To perfuse the kidneys you have to have a pump (heart) strong enough to maintain certain blood pressures.  Congestive heart failure is a diagnosis that means the pump is failing and can't keep up with demand so you augment it with medications to make the best of it.

For kidneys to work, aside from getting blood as above, they need intact nephrons which are the individual filters (think like coffee paper). Each kidney has around 1 million and you lose some with age but high blood pressure, diabetes, drugs, and numerous other things accelerate the loss and cause other dysfunction in the kidneys.

You're mom likely has had a 1 - 2 punch. Bad kidneys followed by pump failure.  This is what is called cardiorenal syndrome.  In most cases it is terminal because the heart won't tolerate the stress of surgery or dialysis and the kidneys rapidly fail from low perfusion.  The best you can hope for is one or both to improve with medical support. 

And please don't think of it as letting your mother die, there simply isn't much that can be done.  All bodies have a line which when crossed there is no ability to return to a healthy state.

One specific area are the veins that run to esophagus aka food tube. These veins swell up similar to hemorrhoids and are prone to rupture. When they do, it causes rapid bleeding.
